title: Also everyone should go listen to the “Liz Swados Project” album beca...
transcript: Before Oh Mary and Rocky Horror, Tony winner Sam Pinkleton took on a very different project, directing an ensemble of young actors, including future stars like Michaela Jae Rodriguez and Sophia Ann Caruso, in a very rare revival of a fascinating musical that you might not have heard of. After a brief hiatus, welcome to the return of my series Overthinking Theatre Throwback, where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history. In 1978, following somewhat on the heels of musicals like Hair and a Chorus Line, the Public Theatre put on a brand new musical called Runaways. It wasn't about hippies or dancers, but rather a group of children and adolescents who had run away from broken homes. And the large cast consisted of actual children and adolescents, some of whom were the real life runaways who had participate in the workshops and research sessions for the show. Runaways was the brain child of groundbreaking musical theatre composer Elizabeth Swados. And listen to me, if you are at all a fan of indie alternative musical theatre like Dave Malloy, Heather Christian, the Bengsons, Elizabeth Swados is absolutely a name you should know because she was a trailblazer for all of them. She was also an underappreciated queer icon in the theatre Happy Pride everyone! and Runaways was probably her most high profile achievement. It was an exuberant patchwork quilt of songs, stories and poems with a very eclectic blend of music styles to reflect the diverse identities and experiences of the characters. The show quickly transferred from the Public to Broadway, getting nominated at the Tonys in five pretty major categories, including Best Musical. But it closed after only about seven months. And presumably because of the nature of the show and the casting, it has barely been performed professionally since. But cut forward several decades, and honestly, this might deserve a throwback video of its own, but back in the 2010s there used to be a spin-off program of the Encores Series called Encores Off-Center They did the same kind of concert revivals of musicals that had, shall we say, a more downtown vibe. And one such revival was, you guessed it, Runaways, only a few months after Liz Swados's untimely death at age 64. And let me tell you, I saw this production from the front row and it rocked me to my core. It was one of the most exhilarating theatrical experiences I've ever had. There was something so raw and primal about it. It captured the daily struggles, the escapist joy, and above all else, the burning frustration of these children who have been left to fend for themselves. One of the most tragic things about it is how they're so desperate to be understood, even when many of them are too young to even really understand themselves the scope of the trauma that they're working out in what feels like real time. I really wish there had been a cast album made of this production. there is one of the original, but in my opinion it doesn't really capture the feel of the show. So even more so than the original, this concert revival came and went in a blip. And Runaways overall has continued to be an underappreciated gem in the canon, as has much of the work of Elizabeth Swados.
